v.why: Adding the input-to-output residual is a large gain when e3 was empty, but only marginal when it replaces conv or pool (#11,14,15,18 vs #12,13).
Filling an empty direct input-output edge adds a path and helps strongly, whereas replacing an existing skip or pool is neutral or harmful (#19,21,22,23 vs #20,24).
With e1 empty, deleting e0 cuts every conv path into nodes 1 and 2, causing a collapse (#28) far worse than the usual small loss (#25-27).
With e4 empty, e5 is the only conv path into the output, so removing it is very costly (#55 vs #53,54,56).
Without the e3 residual the cell depends more on the node-1 paths, so deleting e0 hurts more (#32 vs #25).
Strengthening the first conv edge matters more when there is no residual shortcut to the output (#44 vs #43, #74 vs #71).
Adding or upgrading the conv into the output gains more in cells lacking the e3 skip (#48 vs #47, #7 vs #1).
A skip on e1 partially supplies the missing residual when e3 is empty, but is useless or harmful when e3 already has a skip (#82 vs #81).
A skip on e4 restores residual-like gradient flow only when e3 lacks a skip (#86 vs #85).
Even a parameter-free pool on e3 helps when it fills an empty edge, but hurts when it replaces the skip (#76 vs #75).

raw:
I looked for edits whose effect changes direction or size depending on a parent condition, across all three datasets.

**Pattern 1: edge 3 is the dominant moderator.**
- **Replacing `none` on edge 3 helps a lot.** Filling e3 with skip, conv or pool when it is `none` gives large gains (#11, 14, 15, 18, 19, 21, 76). Replacing an existing skip or avg_pool there is neutral or harmful (#12, 13, 20, 24, 75).
- **With no skip on edge 3, conv and skip edits elsewhere help more.** Upgrades to conv_3x3 or skip on other edges give clearly bigger gains when e3=`none`. The paired comparisons are #43/44, #71/74, #47/48, #1/7, #81/82 and #85/86, especially on ImageNet16.

**Pattern 2: removing a conv that is the only path through the cell is costly.**
- **Edge 0 when edge 1 is empty.** Deleting e0 when e1=`none` leaves node 2 with no conv input path, giving −6.8/−13.6/−17.1 (#28). With e1 present the cost is about −0.1 to −3 (#25–27).
- **Edge 5 when edge 4 is empty.** Deleting e5 when e4=`none` gives −6.8/−14.1/−17.5 (#55), versus small losses otherwise (#53, 54, 56–58).
- **Edge 0 when edge 3 is empty.** Deleting e0 when e3=`none` costs more because there is no residual to fall back on (#32 vs #25).

**Caveat:** the e3=`none` effects reverse in conv-free cells (all-skip or all-pool, #16, 17). I expect conv-containing cells to dominate the space, but that is the main risk to hypotheses 1, 6, 7, 8 and 9.
